title: Final review of the Phase 3 diff
description:
Review the whole epic diff outside-in before closeout. Phase 2's review (tick oun) declared correct code that then failed twelve different ways in production, so weight this review toward the boundaries that suite green cannot see: platform limits, credential scope, untrusted input, and any config cell read by two runtimes.

Specific things Phase 3 introduces that deserve a named pass:
- Untrusted content: GitHub issue bodies and webhook payloads reach a channel a human acts on. Look for spoofing of the channel's own formatting and for payload text treated as instructions.
- Consent: the tk label boundary, and that removing it actually stops ingestion.
- Write safety: the DO inbox's ordering guarantee under real concurrency, not just its unit tests.
- Provenance: that an approval can never be attributed to the wrong project's gate.
